gloss: be wide, broad; make room, enlarge; breadth; open square
summary: Width and room: the breadth of an ark, an altar or a land measured beside its length, a land “broad of hands” with room on every side, and the open square of a town where its people gathered. The hiphil makes wide: Yahweh enlarges Israel's borders as he swore to the fathers, and “makes room” for the one hemmed in, so that the broad place (מֶרְחָב) is the opposite of the strait (צַר, מֵצַר) and is deliverance; a mouth opened wide boasts or is filled, a heart made wide runs in Yahweh's way, but a heart or soul that is wide is proud and greedy, and the grave widens its throat and is never filled. Arabic raḥuba “be ample”, Ugaritic rḥb “wide”, Ge'ez rəḥba “be wide”, Phoenician yrḥb “I enlarged (the territory)” and Akkadian rebītu “city square” all carry the same sense.

words.summary: About a hundred times, nearly all in measurements, beside אֹרֶךְ “length” and often קוֹמָה “height”: the ark of Noah, the ark of the covenant, the tabernacle and its altar, Solomon's house, and above all the temple and the land of Ezekiel 40–48.

senses.definition: The measure across a thing, set beside its length (and height), in cubits or reeds.

evidence.note: “Three hundred cubits the length of the ark, fifty cubits רָחְבָּהּ, and thirty cubits its height.”
The ark of the covenant: two and a half cubits its length, a cubit and a half רָחְבּוֹ, a cubit and a half its height.
The court: length a hundred cubits, “and breadth fifty by fifty”.
Og's iron bed: nine cubits its length and four cubits its breadth.
Solomon's bronze platform: five cubits long, five cubits wide, three cubits high.
The man with the measuring reed “measured the breadth of the building, one reed, and the height, one reed”.
The holy portion of the land: length twenty-five thousand, “and breadth ten thousand”.
The portion with the sanctuary in its midst: twenty-five thousand in breadth.
“To measure Jerusalem, to see what is רָחְבָּהּ and what is its length.”
The flying scroll: twenty cubits its length and ten cubits its breadth.

senses.gloss: breadth, extent (of a land, of waters)
senses.definition: The whole spread of a land or of waters, from side to side.

evidence.note: “Arise, walk through the land לְאָרְכָּהּ וּלְרָחְבָּהּ, for to you I will give it.”
The Assyrian flood: “the spreading of his wings shall fill the breadth of your land, Immanuel.”
“By the breath of God ice is given, and the breadth of the waters is made fast.”

senses.definition: Of Solomon: a wide reach of understanding, set with wisdom and discernment.

evidence.note: “God gave Solomon wisdom and discernment very great, וְרֹחַב לֵב like the sand on the shore of the sea.”

evidence.locator: Exo.26.16 and elsewhere, רֹחַב → πλάτος; πλάτος renders רֹחַב ×22, εὖρος ×19

evidence.note: The holy city lies foursquare, “its length as great as its breadth (πλάτος)”, measured with a reed, as Ezekiel's temple and land and Zechariah's Jerusalem were.
“To comprehend … what is the breadth (πλάτος) and length and depth and height.”

parallels.note: “Length”: the fixed partner in every measurement.

words.gloss: open square, broad place of a town; street
words.summary: The broad open place of a town, often by its gate, where strangers spent the night, the people assembled, the elders sat and the law was read; in the plural, the squares and streets of a city, set beside חוּצוֹת “streets, outside”. Arabic raḥabah “open court” and Akkadian rebītu “city square” are the same word.

senses.definition: The one broad open place of a town, by its gate, where people gathered, sat in judgment, heard the law, or, without a host, spent the night.

evidence.note: “All the people gathered as one man אֶל־הָרְחוֹב that was before the Water Gate”, and Ezra read the law there.
Hezekiah gathered the captains “to the square of the gate of the city” and spoke to their heart.
“When I went out to the gate by the city, בָּרְחוֹב I prepared my seat.”
The two messengers to Lot: “No, but we will spend the night בָרְחוֹב.”
The Levite “sat down in the square of the city, and no man took them into his house to lodge”.
The spoil of a city gone after other gods is gathered “into the midst of its square” and burnt.
The people sat “in the square of the house of God”, trembling because of the rain.
The man the king delights to honour is led on horseback “through the square of the city”.
From the word to restore and build Jerusalem: “it shall be built again, רְחוֹב and moat, in troubled times.”

senses.definition: In the plural, the open places and streets of a city, where its life is seen: mourning, children playing, wisdom calling, the dead and the starving.

evidence.note: “Run to and fro בְּחוּצוֹת Jerusalem … and seek בִרְחוֹבוֹתֶיהָ, if you can find a man who does justice.”
“In all רְחֹבוֹת wailing, and in all חוּצוֹת they shall say, Alas! alas!”
“Wisdom cries aloud בַּחוּץ, בָּרְחֹבוֹת she gives her voice.”
“Old men and old women shall again sit in the squares of Jerusalem … and the squares of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in its squares.”
Child and suckling faint “in the squares of the town”.
The chariots rage בַּחוּצוֹת and jostle בָּרְחֹבוֹת of Nineveh.
“Truth has stumbled in the square, and uprightness cannot enter.”
The sluggard: “A lion outside! I shall be killed in the midst of the squares.”
Jerusalem's harlotry: “you made yourself a high place in every square.”
“No outcry in our squares.”

evidence.locator: Gen.19.2, בָרְחוֹב → ἐν τῇ πλατείᾳ; Ezr.10.9; Neh.8.16 → πλατείαις; πλατεῖα renders רְחוֹב ×26

evidence.note: “Go out quickly into the streets (πλατείας) and lanes of the city.”
“The street (πλατεῖα) of the city was pure gold”: the squares of the holy city, as in Zec 8:4–5.

parallels.note: “Outside, street”: the plural חוּצוֹת is the regular partner of רְחֹבוֹת.

words.gloss: wide, broad, spacious; (of heart or soul) proud, greedy
words.summary: Wide: a land with room on every side, a broad wall, a wide cup, the sea, a commandment. Said of the heart or the soul, it is the man who takes up room: “wide of heart” stands with “high of eyes” for pride, and “wide of soul” is the greedy man who stirs up strife. The BDB key also counts the six tokens of the name Rahab (names/rahab.json).

senses.gloss: spacious, with room (of a land, a city)
senses.definition: Of a land or a city: wide and roomy, with space for more people; often רַחֲבַת יָדַיִם “broad of hands”, wide on both sides.

evidence.note: “Let them dwell in the land and trade in it, for the land, behold, רַחֲבַת־יָדַיִם before them.”
“A people secure, and the land broad of hands … a place where there is no lack of anything.”
“Fat and good pasture, and the land broad of hands, quiet and peaceful.”
“The city was broad of hands and great, and the people few within it, and no houses built.”
Yahweh came down to bring Israel up “to a land good and broad, a land flowing with milk and honey”.
“In the broad and fat land that you gave before them they did not serve you.”
Shebna tossed like a ball “into a land broad of hands”.
Yahweh in majesty for Zion, “a place of rivers, streams broad of hands”, where no galley goes.
“This sea, great and broad of hands; there are creeping things without number.”

senses.gloss: wide, broad (of a wall, a cup, a breach)
senses.definition: Of a made or measured thing: wide across.

evidence.note: They restored Jerusalem “as far as the Broad Wall (הַחוֹמָה הָרְחָבָה)”.
“The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly overthrown.”
“Your sister's cup you shall drink, deep and wide, holding much.”
“As through a wide breach they come.”
The measure of God's ways is “longer than the earth and broader than the sea”.
“The work is great and wide, and we are spread out on the wall, far from one another.”
“To all perfection I have seen an end; רְחָבָה מִצְוָתְךָ מְאֹד”: your commandment has no end to its breadth.

senses.gloss: at large, in a wide place (בָרְחָבָה)
senses.definition: As a noun with בְּ: in open space, unhemmed, the walk of one who seeks Yahweh's precepts.

evidence.note: “And I will walk בָרְחָבָה, for I have sought your precepts.”

senses.gloss: wide of heart, wide of soul: proud, greedy
senses.definition: With לֵב or נֶפֶשׁ: one whose heart or appetite takes up room, set with high eyes for pride and against trust in Yahweh for greed.

evidence.note: “גְּבַהּ־עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵבָב, him I will not endure.”
“רוּם־עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב־לֵב, the lamp of the wicked, is sin.”
“רְחַב־נֶפֶשׁ stirs up strife, but he who trusts in Yahweh will be made fat.”
“Wide (πλατεῖα) is the gate and broad the way that leads to destruction.”

opposites.note: “Trust (in Yahweh)”: the opposite of the man wide of soul.

phrases.gloss: broad of hands, spacious on both sides

words.gloss: be wide; (hiphil) make wide, enlarge, make room
words.summary: Twenty-five times, nearly all hiphil. Yahweh widens the borders of Israel and makes room for his people and for the one in distress; the mouth is opened wide against an enemy or to be filled; the heart is made wide to run in Yahweh's way; and the grave and the arrogant man widen their throat (נֶפֶשׁ) and are not filled. Phoenician uses the same verb of a king who “enlarged” his territory.

senses.definition: Of a building, to grow wider upward; of the mouth, to be opened wide over enemies; of the heart, to swell with joy.

evidence.note: The side chambers “grew wider (וְרָחֲבָה) as they went up”, so the house was broader above.
Hannah: “My heart exults in Yahweh … רָחַב פִּי over my enemies, for I rejoice in your salvation.”
“Then you shall see and be radiant, and your heart shall thrill and grow wide, for the abundance of the sea shall be turned to you.”

senses.definition: Of pasture: wide, with room to graze.

evidence.note: “In that day your cattle shall graze in a pasture נִרְחָב.”

stems.gloss: make wide, enlarge; make room, set free; open wide

senses.definition: To widen the territory of a people, as Yahweh promised Israel; of Ammon, by violence.

evidence.note: “I will drive out nations before you וְהִרְחַבְתִּי אֶת־גְּבוּלֶךָ.”
“If Yahweh your God enlarges your border, as he swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land he promised to give to your fathers.”
“When Yahweh your God enlarges your border as he promised you.”
Ammon ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead “that they might enlarge their border”.
“Blessed is he who enlarges Gad.”

senses.definition: To give room to one crowded or hemmed in: room to dwell, room for the step, relief in distress.

evidence.note: Over the third well there was no quarrel, “and he called its name Rehoboth, and said, For now Yahweh הִרְחִיב לָנוּ, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”
“In distress (בַּצָּר) you made room for me (הִרְחַבְתָּ לִּי).”
“You enlarge my step under me, and my ankles have not slipped” (also Psa 18:37).
“A man's gift makes room for him, and brings him before the great.”
“The distresses of my heart הִרְחִיבוּ; bring me out of my straits”: the troubles have grown wide, or, pointed as an imperative, “relieve the distresses of my heart”.

senses.definition: To open the mouth wide: in mockery against someone, or to be filled.

evidence.note: “They open their mouth wide against me; they say, Aha, aha, our eye has seen it.”
“Against whom do you open the mouth wide and stretch out the tongue?”
“I am Yahweh your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt; הַרְחֶב־פִּיךָ and I will fill it.”

senses.gloss: make wide the heart; widen the throat (appetite)
senses.definition: With לֵב, to make the heart wide, free and ready; with נֶפֶשׁ, to open wide the throat or appetite, as the grave does that is never filled.

evidence.note: “The way of your commandments I will run, for you make my heart wide.”
“Therefore the grave (שְׁאוֹל) has widened its throat (נַפְשָׁהּ) and opened its mouth without measure.”
The proud man “who widens his throat like the grave, and is like death, and is not satisfied, and gathers to himself all nations”.

senses.definition: To widen a tent's place, a bed, a pyre, a shaven patch.

evidence.note: “Make wide the place of your tent, and let the curtains of your dwellings be stretched out.”
“You uncovered yourself and went up; you made your bed wide.”
“Make your baldness wide as the eagle, for they have gone into exile from you.”
Tophet: “he has made its pyre deep and wide, fire and much wood.”

evidence.locator: Gen.26.22, הִרְחִיב → ἐπλάτυνεν; Psa.119.32, תַרְחִיב → ἐπλάτυνας; Exo.34.24 → πλατύνω; πλατύνω and ἐμπλατύνω render רָחַב ×20

evidence.note: “Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians; our heart is made wide (πεπλάτυνται)”: the wide heart of Psa 119:32.
“Be made wide (πλατύνθητε) you also.”
“They make broad their phylacteries.”

parallels.note: “Open wide (the mouth)”: of the grave, with “widen its throat”.
“Lengthen”: the tent's cords lengthened as its place is widened; the tongue stretched out as the mouth is opened.

opposites.note: “Distress, strait”: Yahweh makes room in it.
“Be satisfied”: the widened throat of the grave and the proud man is not.

words.summary: Six times: the open space into which Yahweh brings out the one he delivers, the opposite of the strait (מֵצַר), and the wide open country.

senses.definition: Open room, where one is no longer hemmed in by enemies or distress: where Yahweh brings and sets the one he saves.

evidence.note: “From the strait (הַמֵּצַר) I called on Yah; Yah answered me בַמֶּרְחָב.”
“He brought me out לַמֶּרְחָב; he delivered me, because he delighted in me” (also 2Sa 22:20).
“You have not shut me up in the hand of the enemy; you have set my feet בַמֶּרְחָב.”

senses.gloss: open country, breadths of the earth
senses.definition: Wide open land: pasture, or the earth's whole breadth.

evidence.note: “Israel is stubborn like a stubborn heifer; now will Yahweh pasture them like a lamb בַּמֶּרְחָב?”
The Chaldeans, “who march through the breadths of the earth to possess dwellings not theirs”.

opposites.note: “Strait, distress”: called from, answered in the broad place.

words.summary: Three times in Job and Isaiah; two of BDB's three are spelled as the construct plural of the adjective (Isa 33:21, Job 38:18) and are counted under both. Its one sure use is Job 36:16.

senses.definition: Room with no constraint; in the plural, the wide spaces of the earth.

evidence.note: “He has drawn you out of the mouth of distress (צָר) רַחַב, with no constraint beneath it.”
“Have you understood the breadths of the earth (רַחֲבֵי־אָרֶץ)? Declare, if you know it all.”

words.summary: The name of a well of Isaac, explained from the verb: “for now Yahweh has made room (הִרְחִיב) for us” (Gen 26:22); also Rehoboth-Ir, built with Nineveh (Gen 10:11), and Rehoboth “on the river”, the city of Shaul king of Edom (Gen 36:37; 1Ch 1:48). The spelling is the plural of רְחוֹב, and BDB's key also takes plural tokens of that noun (Jer 9:20, Amo 5:16, Pro 22:13). Places, so no name entry.

senses.definition: A well dug by Isaac's servants in the land of Gerar, and two towns of the name.

evidence.note: “They did not quarrel over it, and he called its name רְחֹבוֹת, and said, For now Yahweh הִרְחִיב לָנוּ.”
“He built Nineveh, and רְחֹבֹת עִיר, and Calah.”
“Shaul of Rehoboth on the River reigned in his place.”

words.summary: Towns: Rehob at the far north of the land the spies explored, “at Lebo-hamath” (Num 13:21), and Beth-rehob, in whose valley Dan stood (Jdg 18:28) and whose Arameans Ammon hired (2Sa 10:6, 8); and Rehob of Asher, a Levitical city (Jos 19:28, 30; 21:31; Jdg 1:31; 1Ch 6:60). The spelling is the noun רְחוֹב. The name is also borne by two men, in names/rehob.json; BDB's key also takes common-noun tokens (Ezk 16:24, 31; Est 4:6; Dan 9:25; 2Ch 32:6). Places, so no name entry for them.

senses.definition: Towns of the name: one at the northern limit of the land, near Lebo-hamath (Beth-rehob), and one in Asher.

evidence.note: “They spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, at Lebo-hamath.”
Laish lay “in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob”.
“Aram of Zobah and of Rehob”.
In the border of Asher.
Given with its pasturelands to the Levites.
Asher did not drive out the dwellers of Rehob.

cognates.form: رَحُبَ، رَحِبَ، أَرْحَبَ، رَحْبٌ، رُحْبٌ، مَرْحَبٌ
cognates.translit: raḥuba, raḥiba, ʾarḥaba, raḥb, ruḥb, marḥab
cognates.gloss: be ample, spacious, wide, roomy; (IV) make wide; (raḥb) wide; (ruḥb) ampleness; (raḥbu ṣ-ṣadr) wide of breast: free from distress, liberal; (marḥaban) “ampleness, not straitness”: welcome
cognates.note: The same sense through every form: a land or road wide and roomy, a wound made wide, a man “ample in the breast” free from distress of mind, and the greeting marḥaban, “you have come to ampleness, not straitness”, the מֶרְחָב set against מֵצַר of Psa 118:5. Arabic shows ḥ behind ח.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1051, art. رحب, رَحُبَ (n15020)
evidence.note: “It was, or became, ample, spacious, wide, or roomy”; IV ارحبهُ “He made it ample, spacious, wide, or roomy”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1051, art. رحب, رَحْبٌ (n15021)
evidence.note: “Ample, spacious, wide, or roomy; applied to a place … رَجُلٌ رَحْبُ الصَّدْر A man ample, or dilated, in the breast.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1052, art. رحب, مَرْحَبٌ (n15031)
evidence.note: مَرْحَبًا “Thou hast come to, or found, ampleness, spaciousness, or roominess; not straitness.”

cognates.gloss: court, open area, spacious vacant part of a mosque, house or place; open ground among houses
cognates.note: The open place within a settlement, “so called because of its ampleness”: the רְחוֹב of a town.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1051, art. رحب, رَحَبَةٌ (n15024)
evidence.note: “The court, open area, or spacious vacant part or portion, of a mosque, and of a house, or of a place; so called because of its ampleness: and in like manner, between, or among, houses.”
“wide, broad, spacious”; compares Hebrew רָחָב, Arabic رَحْب.

cognates.gloss: be wide; (causative) widen, enlarge, make room, open wide; (rəḥub) wide, spacious, broad; (rāḥb) breadth, width
cognates.note: The Ge'ez Bible uses the causative where the Hebrew has the hiphil (Gen 26:22, Deu 12:20, Isa 54:2, Psa 4:1 and 119:32 in its numbering), and rāḥb for רֹחַב; that is a translation, but the root's own range in Ge'ez is the same: be wide, widen, open (the mouth, the heart) wide. Ge'ez ሐ shows ḥ behind ח.

evidence.note: ʾarḥaba “widen, enlarge, broaden, make room (for), open wide, extend, amplify”; tarəḥba “be enlarged, be widened”; rəḥub “wide, spacious, broad, ample, extensive”.

evidence.locator: s.v. ረሐበ: አርሐበ, ተርሕበ, ርሑብ, ራሕብ
evidence.note: አርሐበ “latum, amplum, spatiosum facere, dilatare … late aperire, os … cor”; ርሑብ “latus, amplus, spatiosus”; ራሕብ “amplitudo, latitudo”.

cognates.note: Azatiwada at Karatepe: “I enlarged the land of the Vale of Adana from the rising of the sun to its setting”, the very use of Exo 34:24 and Deu 12:20, a king widening his border.

evidence.note: yrḥb ʾnk ʾrṣ ʿmq ʾdn lmmṣʾ šmš wʿd mbʾy, “I enlarged the territory of the Vale of Adana from East to West.”

cognates.note: Sabaean (Old South Arabian): width in a measurement, “thirty-five cubits in height and fourteen cubits in width”, as רֹחַב is used; and rḥbt, the wide low country, as מֶרְחָב of open land. South Arabian ḥ shows ḥ behind ח.

evidence.locator: p. 485, RḤB (rḥbm “width”, C 541/109–10; rḥbtn “plain, flatland or lowland”, C 540/68)

cognates.gloss: city square, open space; street; quarter
cognates.note: Akkadian loses ḥ and colours the vowel to e (as rēmu “womb” beside רֶחֶם), so rebītu answers to רְחוֹב: the open square of a city.

evidence.note: “city square; open space; quarter; square; street”.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the Targum of Pro 28:25 keeps the Hebrew's figure, a man wide (of soul) is the greedy man.

evidence.locator: s.v. רְחַב (ch.), citing Targ. Prov. XXVIII, 25
evidence.note: “esp. (with or sub. נפשא) ambitious, greedy.”

doctrine.statement: Yahweh told Abram, “all the land that you see, to you I will give it and to your seed for ever … arise, walk through the land in its length and in its breadth (וּלְרָחְבָּהּ), for to you I will give it” (Gen 13:15, 17); the promise is of a land with measurable breadth, to be walked over. When Isaac's well was at last uncontested he named it Rehoboth, “for now Yahweh has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land” (Gen 26:22), and Yahweh then renewed the oath to him (Gen 26:3–4, 24). Moses tells Israel that Yahweh will “enlarge your border, as he swore to your fathers, and give you all the land he promised to give to your fathers” (Deu 19:8; Exo 34:24; Deu 12:20). Yet Stephen says Abraham was given “no inheritance in it, not even a foot's length, but he promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him” (Act 7:5), and Hebrews that Abraham sojourned “in the land of promise as in a foreign land”, and that he and all the faithful “died in faith, not having received the promises”, so that “apart from us they should not be made perfect” (Heb 11:9, 13, 39–40). From the verses: the land promised to Abraham in its length and breadth was promised to him personally, he has not yet received it, and he will receive it with the faithful together, which requires his resurrection.

Isaiah says “the grave (שְׁאוֹל) has widened its throat (הִרְחִיבָה … נַפְשָׁהּ) and opened its mouth without measure, and her glory and her multitude … go down into it” (Isa 5:14), and Habakkuk says the proud man “widens his throat like the grave, and is like death, and is not satisfied” (Hab 2:5). The grave is pictured as a mouth and throat that swallows men and is never full: “the grave and destruction are never satisfied” (Pro 27:20), it is one of the things that never say “Enough” (Pro 30:15–16). Here נֶפֶשׁ is the throat and appetite, set beside “mouth”, and it is the grave's own. From the verses: the grave is the place where the dead are swallowed up, not a place of life; and נֶפֶשׁ in scripture's own use can be a throat or an appetite, which is no immortal part of man.

Isaiah calls the barren woman to sing, “for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife”, and then, “make wide (הַרְחִיבִי) the place of your tent … lengthen your cords and strengthen your stakes, for you shall spread out to the right and to the left, and your seed shall possess the nations and make the desolate cities inhabited” (Isa 54:1–3). Paul quotes Isa 54:1 of “the Jerusalem above”, “the mother of us all”, and concludes, “we, brothers, as Isaac was, are children of promise” (Gal 4:26–28); he has already said that those who are Christ's are “Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise” (Gal 3:29). From the verses: the widened tent is room made for the many children of promise, who are Abraham's seed by belonging to Christ, and their inheritance is the possession of the nations and the resettling of the desolate cities on the earth.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18 from the brief. Names in their own files: Rahab (t.bw.ae), Rehoboam (t.bw.aj), Rehabiah (t.bw.ai), and Rehob for the two men of that name (no bdb key: t.bw.ag, which also holds the town and common-noun tokens, stays here on the place-name word). The adjective's key t.bw.ad also counts the six Rahab tokens by spelling, and t.bw.ab (רַחַב) shares Isa 33:21 and Job 38:18 with the adjective. Beth-rehob (b.bp.bt) is filed under בית and left there; m.dl.ab (מֶרְחַבְיָה, a zero-token cross-reference) is not entered. Not this root: Rahab the sea monster and Egypt (רַהַב, Job 9:13, Isa 51:9, Psa 87:4), root רהב. No Biblical Aramaic word of the root (Daniel and Ezra use פְּתָי for breadth); the Peshitta has the root only in the names Rahab (SEDRA lexeme 2990, Mat 1:5, Heb 11:31, Jas 2:25) and Rehoboam (lexeme 2991, Mat 1:7). Not consulted: Payne Smith for a Syriac rḥb (none in SEDRA's NT); DULAT and Segert for Ugaritic rḥb (Segert's glossary lists only the place name rhbn; Wiktionary also has rḥbt “amphora”, perhaps “the wide one”, not entered); CAD R for rebītu (cited from Oracc); Dillmann's column for ረሐበ (the TraCES data gives the article, not the column). Open: (1) Psa 25:17 הִרְחִיבוּ is read either as “the distresses of my heart have grown wide” or, repointed, “relieve the distresses of my heart”; it is cited under make-room with both readings, not as defining. (2) The seed-of-promise doctrine rests on Paul's quotation of Isa 54:1, the verse before the one using the root; the reviewer may prefer to drop it or fold it into land-promise. (3) Klein connects the root with רוח “be spacious”; not followed.
